subject.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention

question: Should LINE expose bounded pending-media retention as an explicitly best-effort, process-local configuration contract?
rationale: The opt-in gate direction has prior support, but the new queue retains user media for a later turn while intentionally losing that association on restart; implementation review cannot decide whether that lifecycle should become a public channel contract.

options.title: Approve best-effort retention
options.body: Keep the bounded process-local queue after the race is fixed, with restart and TTL limitations clearly documented and proven.

options.title: Require durable retention
options.body: Persist pending-media metadata in an approved SQLite owner so queued user media survives gateway restarts until delivery or expiry.

options.title: Remove the retention queue
options.body: Narrow the change to non-text gating only if maintainers do not want to own retained-media state and lifecycle behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve best-effort retention
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded process-local queue after the race is fixed, with restart and TTL limitations clearly documented and proven.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the canonical LINE mention-gating behavior and are the strongest available history signal for deciding whether this extension becomes a supported contract.
